paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: guilt doesn't wait for you to notice it. When someone breaks one of the LORD's commandments without knowing it, the LORD still counts him guilty (Leviticus 5:17). The passage closes that case with, "he was certainly guilty before the LORD." (Leviticus 5:19). So the LORD takes sin seriously, even the sin you never saw coming.

Now look at what the LORD calls cheating a neighbor. Lying about something left in his care, or swearing falsely about lost property, is acting unfaithfully against the LORD (Leviticus 6:2-3). It's not just a problem between two people. And the making right starts fast: he returns what he took, adds a fifth, and pays the owner on the day he acknowledges his guilt (Leviticus 6:4-5). No "I'll get to it after the next batch," friend, I've said that about dishes and it never ends well.

Here's the good news, and it's the heart of it. After he makes things right, he brings the unblemished ram to the priest, and the priest makes atonement for him (Leviticus 6:6-7). The LORD says "he will be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt." (Leviticus 6:7). So when guilt shows up, bring it into the light, make it right and trust the LORD's forgiveness. And keep that apron on, because the LORD isn't done teaching Moses about the offerings.
